distinct_grid_states:
FOUR distinct grids across everything I read, of which THREE fall inside the 2016-2020 window, and only TWO of those differ on any bound the crate models.

STATE 0 (pre-window, for reference only) — the 2013-08-20 portal capture: Nikkei 225 7.45am-2.25pm / 3.15pm-2.00am; FTSE China A50 9.00am-3.55pm / 4.40pm-2.00am; MSCI Singapore 8.30am-5.10pm / 6.15pm-2.00am; MSCI Taiwan 8.45am-1.45pm / 2.35pm-2.00am; no NTR suite. The 2018-07-11 orphan capture states a FIFTH variant (A50 3.25pm/4.10pm, everything else as state 0) but its contract set proves the content is older still — roughly 2012 — so I do not count it as a published 2018 state at all.

STATE A — spans capture 20170705000242 through capture 20170927124017 (a 12-week interval in which SGX's own hours table did not change by one character; the two parsed tables diff clean). Nikkei 225 7.30 am to 2.25 pm / 2.55 pm to 4.45 am; FTSE China A50 9:00 am to 4:30 pm / 5.00 pm to 4.45 am; MSCI Singapore 8.30am to 5.10 pm / 5.40 pm to 4.45 am; MSCI Taiwan 8.45 am to 1.45 pm / 2.15 pm to 4.45 am. NTR (USD) not listed. Dividend Point (ND) on its own grid, 7.30 am to 5.55 pm / 6.25 pm to 4.45 am.

STATE B — spans artifact date 2018-04-11 (calendar 2018 (Apr)) through 2019-01-22 (calendar 2019), corroborated mid-interval by the 2018-10-30 contract-spec page for the A50. Identical to state A on all four modelled equity-index families; adds the NTR (USD) suite at 7.25am to 6.30pm / 7.00pm to 4.45am, and moves the Dividend Point contract onto the Nikkei grid. So states A and B AGREE on every bound the crate models for Japan, China, Singapore and MSCI Taiwan — i.e. from 2017-07-05 to 2019-01-22, SGX published exactly ONE grid for those families, and the sourced intersection over that stretch is that grid undegraded.

STATE C — artifact date 2020-01-02 (calendar 2020). Nikkei 225 7.30am to 2.25pm / 2.55pm to 5.15am; FTSE China A50 9.00am to 4.30pm / 5.00pm to 5.15am; MSCI Singapore 8.30am to 5.20pm / 5.50pm to 5.15am; MSCI Taiwan 8.45am to 1.45pm / 2.15pm to 5.15am; NTR (USD) 7.25am to 6.30pm / 7.00pm to 5.15am.

Only two moves separate state A from state C: the universal T+1 close 4.45am -> 5.15am, and the SiMSCI-only pair (T close 5.10pm -> 5.20pm, T+1 open 5.40pm -> 5.50pm). Nothing I retrieved witnesses the intermediate 2.00am -> 4.45am step: 4.45am is already in force in SGX's own table at capture 20170705000242, the earliest in-window hours artifact that exists.
dead_ends:
1. THE 2016 AND 2017 CALENDAR PDFs ARE GONE. The 2017-07-05 portal page links six SGX documents by name: SGX+Derivatives+Trading+Calendar+2016_Oct+end+Update_FA.PDF, SGX+Derivatives+Trading+Calendar+2015_Aug+Update_FA.PDF, SGX+Derivatives+Trading+Calendar+2014+-+Oct+2014+update_D1.pdf, DTAM+80+of+2016+Year+End+Trading+Schedule_v06.pdf (+ Appendices 1 and 2), and the 2017-09-27 page adds DTAM+85+of+2016+Full+Year+Calendar_2017_v05.pdf (+ Appendix) and SGX_Derivatives+Trading+Calendar+Update+(Sep+2017).PDF; the 2018-10/12 pages add SGX+Derivatives+Trading+Calendar+2018++(Apr+Update).pdf. Per-URL CDX on each returns ZERO rows — none is in the Wayback Machine. Live, every www.sgx.com/wps/wcm/connect/... path now returns the same 11,792-byte SPA shell (HTTP 200, text/html). Guessed api2.sgx.com/sites/default/files/<YYYY-MM>/ paths for the 2016 and Sep-2017 calendars all 404. Saved as cdx_wcm_dtam.json / cdx_sgx_cal.json.

2. NO SGX DERIVATIVES HOURS PAGE IS ARCHIVED FOR ANY DATE IN 2016. cdx_th_2015_2019.json enumerates every sgx.com URL matching "trading.hours" captured 2015-2019: the derivatives hours page appears at 2013-08-20, then not again until 2017-07-05 (Chinese site) and 2017-09-27 (English site). The 2015-09-24 and 2016-01-08 captures are the SECURITIES page, not derivatives. So 2016 is a genuine hole, not a search failure.

3. SGX MONTHLY MARKET STATISTICS REPORT - MAR 2016 IS LISTED BUT UNREPLAYABLE. Its only capture (20220120065754) returns the SPA shell, not the PDF, because the wcm path had already died by 2022. Same for the Jun/Jul/Oct 2015 reports (captured 2023-2025). Only the Feb-2017 report (captured 2018-09-21, while the path still worked) actually replays. That is why my earliest artifact naming four of the five families is Feb 2017 and not 2016.

4. THE NEW SGX SITE'S PRODUCT PAGES ARE ARCHIVED AS EMPTY SHELLS. www.sgx.com/derivatives/products/chinaa50 (2019-01-16), .../nikkei225futuresoptions?cc=NK (2019-09-22), .../sgxsimsci?cc=SGP (2019-09-30), .../sgxsimsci (2020-09-24) and .../timsci?cc=TW (2021-01-25) all replay as the React shell; the api2.sgx.com/content-api response that carries the contract specification was never archived. Four files kept so the negative is reproducible. The 2018-10-30 capture of the OLD portal's chinaa50/contracts page is the only contract-spec page in the window that actually contains data — the old portal was server-rendered.

5. NO SGX NEWS RELEASE FOR THE JAPAN / SINGAPORE / AUSTRALIA NTR (USD) CONTRACTS. cdx_newsreleases.json enumerates 411 rows under sgx.com/wps/wcm/connect/sgx_en/home/higlights/news_releases; the only NTR items are the 2017-06-12 launch (Taiwan, China Free, India, Indonesia) and the 2017-11-13 EM/EM-Asia release. NSG (SGX MSCI Singapore Free NTR (USD) Index Futures) therefore has no launch artifact I could find; its earliest listing is the 2018 (Apr) calendar.

6. THE ENGLISH FTSE TAIWAN PRESS RELEASE IS NOT ARCHIVED. www.sgx.com/media-centre/20200701-sgx-introduce-sgx-ftse-taiwan-index-futures has zero CDX rows; live it returns 200 but with an empty SPA shell (no _sgxComApp_pageData). Only the zh-hans rendering was archived, and it carries the full article record — same dateArticle, same English metaDescription. I used that.

7. NO SGX FTSE TAIWAN PRODUCT PAGE IS ARCHIVED AT ALL (cdx_ftsetaiwan_prod.json returns four rows, all media-centre or market-update articles).

8. PREMISE CORRECTION, not a dead end but worth flagging: the task asks for "SGX MSCI Singapore Index Futures AND ITS FTSE SUCCESSOR". There is no FTSE successor. The 2021 calendar — the first edition after the MSCI licence expiry that deleted SGX MSCI Taiwan Index Futures and Options outright — still carries SGP SGX MSCI Singapore Index Futures, SGPO SGX MSCI Singapore Index Options and NSP SGX MSCI Singapore NTR (USD) Index Futures. No artifact I retrieved names any "SGX FTSE Singapore" contract. SGX's own 2020-05-27 and 2020-06-02 media-centre slugs ("SGX reduces licence agreement MSCI February 2021 continues serve global" and "SGX announces launch Singapore single stock futures and signs MSCI Singapore") point the same way; I did not fetch their bodies because the 2021 calendar settles it directly and is the stronger source.

9. WAYBACK FLAKINESS. web.archive.org intermittently refused TCP connections (curl exit 7) for the first ~4 attempts on many requests during this run. Everything here went through fetch.sh (8 attempts, incremental backoff), which is saved in the channel directory so the retrievals are reproducible.
